newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegalese economy remains fragile - minister.
newsitem.headline: Senegalese economy remains fragile - minister.

text.p: Senegal's economy remains fragile despite recording 5.6 percent Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in 1996 and 4.6 percent in 1995, its Economy Minister Papa Ousmane Sacko said on Friday.
"It is worth highlighting that the results we just recall are important, but the economy remains fragile and must be strengthened," he told a workshop on economic development.

The minister said growth was due mainly to Senegal's traditional exporting sectors such as groundnuts, chemical products and fisheries, but also to the building sector, which is experiencing a boom with Senegalese abroad building at home.
Many have more cash in local terms after a 50 percent devaluation of the CFA franc currency in 1994.

"As far as public finance are concerned, there is a real improvement which is reflected in the reduction of the budget deficit from 5.7 percent of the GDP in 1994 to 3.2 percent in 1995 and 1.9 percent in 1996," Sacko said.
Senegal aims to achieve six percent GDP growth in 1997.
